subject: APAC edge micro‑region capacity & onboarding checklist for OrbitAI (ORBIT-492)
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sylvia Choi <sylvia.choi@orbitai.com>, Nathan Lee <nathan.lee@orbitai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: APAC micro-region capacity planning — quick info needed

Hi Sylvia / Nathan —

Congrats on getting to legal review on ORBIT-492. Before we lock formal reserved capacity for your APAC rollout, a couple quick asks so we size the micro-region pool correctly (edge + central mix):

- Preferred locality: you mentioned Singapore in the call — do we need strict residency (no egress) or is regional (APAC) OK?
- Expected peak concurrent users (chat sessions) and p95 requests per minute (RPM) during the first 3 months and at steady state (6–12 months).
- Average prompt + response token size (or sample prompts) and % of streaming vs non-streaming requests.
- Any expected large-batch embedding or retraining jobs that would run in same pool (we prefer separating inference vs batch).

If you can drop the traffic profile PDF (or numbers) by EOD Tuesday, I’ll circulate an initial sizing + canary plan and a short onboarding checklist (network, KMS, audits). I’ve attached a blank sizing sheet you can paste numbers into.

Thanks — we want to align on a small, low-latency APAC edge pool (L4s) with a warm H100 fallback in the same region to preserve model parity and fallbacks.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0183

Attachments: ORBIT-492_pool_sizing_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Sylvia Choi <sylvia.choi@orbitai.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nathan Lee <nathan.lee@orbitai.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 03:40:00 +0800
Subject: Re: APAC micro-region capacity planning — quick info needed

Hi Hannah —

Thanks — uploaded a short traffic profile (see attachment). Key points:
- Residency: Singapore-only for the first 12 months (legal requires no non-APAC egress for customer data).
- Month 0–3 peak: ~1,200 concurrent chat sessions; p95 RPM ~3,500. Steady state (6–12mo): concurrent 3,500; p95 RPM ~10,000.
- Avg prompt + response: 80 tokens in, 220 tokens out. 30% streaming, 70% non-streaming.
- Embeddings: small nightly batch (50k vectors) — can be scheduled to low-traffic windows; doesn’t need H100.

We want latency under 120ms p95 for new-user flows. Cost is sensitive: OrbitAI is evaluating a 12‑month reserved commitment with quarterly usage reviews.

Attaching orbitai_traffic_profile_jun26.pdf. Happy to hop on a quick call if any numbers need clarifying.

Best,
Sylvia Choi
Head of Platform, OrbitAI
Sylvia.choi@orbitai.com

Attachments: orbitai_traffic_profile_jun26.pdf

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sylvia Choi <sylvia.choi@orbitai.com>, Nathan Lee <nathan.lee@orbitai.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Jul 2026 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: Proposal: Singapore micro-edge + warm H100 fallback (ORBIT-492) — sizing + asks

Team —

Attached is a rapid first-pass based on OrbitAI's profile. High-level recommendation for a Singapore micro-region (data residency requirement + low-latency p95 target):

1) Edge micro-pool (low-latency L4s): 12 x L4 (sustained qps for chat inference)
   - Purpose: handle low-latency interactive sessions (p95 target <120ms).
   - Expected steady-state headroom: ~3,500 concurrent sessions with fair batching; reserve 20% for burst.

2) Warm central pool in same region (H100s): 4 x H100 (fallback for heavy prompts and model parity)
   - Purpose: complex generations, long seqs, can serve as degrade path if edge saturated.

3) Burst allowance: up to additional 8 x L4 via on-demand partner pool (SoutheastCloud) for phased ramp; billed separately but we can include a burst SLA in contract.

4) Storage/KMS/Networking: Singapore KMS key required; no cross-border egress. Need legal sign-off + network peering 2 weeks before canary.

Estimated committed term: 12 months reserved (pay-for-reserved + overage at 60% discount). Ballpark monthly committed GPU cost delta vs hosted: $XX,XXX — will get Marissa to produce pricing table and commit language.

Action items:
- Jonas: feasibility + confirm capacity lead time for 12 L4 + 4 H100 and partner burst integration. Can we meet a 3‑week provisioning SLA?
- Marissa: draft pricing carve (reserved vs burst) and proposed SLA for residency + latency credits.
- Karthik: any operational constraints on autoscaling or hybrid routing for micro pools?

I’ve attached the filled sizing sheet (ORBIT-492_pool_sizing_v1.xlsx) and a short onboarding checklist (apac-onboarding-checklist.md) — Sylvia, Nathan, please confirm any deviations.

— Hannah
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: ORBIT-492_pool_sizing_v1.xlsx, apac-onboarding-checklist.md

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sylvia Choi <sylvia.choi@orbitai.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2026 15:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Proposal: Singapore micro-edge + warm H100 fallback (ORBIT-492) — sizing + asks

Thanks Hannah — this looks reasonable and conservative enough for an initial commit. Quick notes from infra ops: 

- Capacity lead time: 12 L4s + 4 H100s in SG region — 18 business days to reserve and test (including kernel/quantization validation for the model family). We can hit 3 weeks but need early confirmation on model artifacts.
- Residency: we can enforce a Singapore-only routing policy and KMS in-region. Network peering window: plan 72 hours of validation with OrbitAI to ensure no inadvertent egress.
- Autoscaling constraints: micro-edge pools are limited to ±20% instantaneous autoscale to preserve latency SLOs; for larger bursts we rely on partner pool integration (SoutheastCloud). I’ll book the partner contact and confirm IP allowlist steps.

Operational checklist (short):
1) Procurement: signed ORBIT-492 reserved capacity SOW with burst appendix. (Marissa)
2) Security: in-region KMS & SOC2 substatement updated (Legal).
3) Network: peering + firewall rules + test harness (OrbitAI + Redwood) — 72h window.
4) Canary: 3-day canary at 10% traffic -> ramp to 50% -> full cutover. Monitor latency + error-rate regressions.
5) Rollback: automatic fallback to H100 central pool and to hosted model approximation if on-demand partner fails.

I’ll coordinate a provisioning kick-off once Marissa confirms SOW language and OrbitAI signs the residency appendix.

— Jonas
Head of Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
